1. Solve the equation 5x<sup>2</sup> − 48 = 2x<sup>2</sup>.

We have Collect the terms, Divide by 3, Extract the square root,

5x<sup>2</sup> − 48 = 2x<sup>2</sup>.

3x<sup>2</sup> = 48.

x<sup>2</sup> = 16. x = ±4.

The sign ± before the 4, read plus or minus, shows that the root is either + or −. For (+4) × (+4) = 16, and (−4) × (−4) = 16 The square root of any number is positive or negative. Hitherto we have given only the positive value. In this chapter we shall give √ both values. This sign , called the **radical sign** , is used to indicate √ that a root is to be extracted. Thus 4 means the square root of 4 is √

3

required. 4 means the third root of 4 is required; the small figure placed over the radical sign is called the **index** of the root, and shows the root required.
